- When sentiment is negative or shows early signs of decline, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% in early periods.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overreacts — dampen forecast slope by 10–20% in the first 5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, model often underestimates downward moves — add 1–3% buffer to forecast for 3–7 days ahead.
- Forecasting horizon >15 days shows increasing lag — adjust for delayed reaction to sentiment shifts; apply 1–2 day lag correction for sentiment-driven moves.
